simple.meaning: מַחְתָּה (machtâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a pan for live coals.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 22 times across Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, and 2 more, beginning at Exodus 25:38. Its contexts include family line, altar.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַחְתָּה (H4289).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מַחְתָּה (machtâh) / H4289 is traced through Exodus 25:38, Exodus 27:3, Exodus 37:23, Exodus 38:3 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H4289. machtah מַחְתָּה noun feminine fire-holder, censer, snuffdish ; — absolute ׳מ Lev 16:12 ; Num 17:11 ; suffix מַחְתָּתוֺ Lev 10:1 + 4 t.; plural absolute מַחְתּוֺת Num 16:6 4 t.; מַחְתֹּת 16:17 3 t.; construct מַחְתּוֺת 17:3 ; 17:4 ; suffix מַחְתֹּתָיו Exod 27:3 ; מַחְתֹּתֶיהָ 25:38 2 t; — 1 snuff-holder , snuff-dish (Now Archäol. ii, 63. 65 ) of gold Exod 25:38 ; 37:23 ; Num 4:9 (all P). 2 bronze utensils , fire-pans , belonging to altar of burnt-offerings Exod 27:3 ; 38:3 , compare Num 4:14 (all P); fire-pans of gold 1Kin 7:50 2Chr 4:22 ; 2Kin 25:15 = Jer 52:19 . 3 censer , Lev 10:1 ; 16:12 ; Num 16:6 , 17 (4 t. in verse); 16:18 ; 17:2 ; 17:3 ; 17:4 (of bronze), 16:11 (all P). חַתְחַת חִתָּה, see below חתת .

occurrences.englishText: Its snuffers and its snuff dishes shall be of pure gold.
You shall make its pots to take away its ashes; and its shovels, its basins, its meat hooks, and its fire pans. You shall make all its vessels of bronze.
He made its seven lamps, and its snuffers, and its snuff dishes, of pure gold.
He made all the vessels of the altar: the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the fire pans. He made all its vessels of bronze.
Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, each took his censer, and put fire in it, and laid incense on it, and offered strange fire before Yahweh, which he had not commanded them.
He shall take a censer full of coals of fire from off the altar before Yahweh, and two handfuls of sweet incense beaten small, and bring it within the veil.
“They shall take a blue cloth and cover the lamp stand of the light, its lamps, its snuffers, its snuff dishes, and all its oil vessels, with which they minister to it.

They shall put on it all its vessels with which they minister about it, the fire pans, the meat hooks, the shovels, and the basins—all the vessels of the altar; and they shall spread on it a covering of sealskin, and put in its poles.
Do this: have Korah and all his company take censers,
Each man take his censer and put incense on it, and each man bring before Yahweh his censer, two hundred fifty censers; you also, and Aaron, each with his censer.”

They each took his censer, and put fire in it, and laid incense on it, and stood at the door of the Tent of Meeting with Moses and Aaron.
“Speak to the children of Israel, and take rods from them, one for each fathers’ house, of all their princes according to their fathers’ houses, twelve rods. Write each man’s name on his rod.
You shall write Aaron’s name on Levi’s rod. There shall be one rod for each head of their fathers’ houses.
You shall lay them up in the Tent of Meeting before the covenant, where I meet with you.
Moses did so. As Yahweh commanded him, so he did.
